title: One shared object per name with intern()

blocks.text: A string literal lives in the String pool, and every equal literal refers to that one object. A String built at run time, with `new` or from other Strings, is a separate object even when its text is the same. `intern()` returns the pool's object for that text, adding it to the pool if it is not there yet.
Write `canonical(String name)` in `Names`. It returns the pooled String with the same text as `name`, so that equal names become one shared object:

items: `canonical(new String("Hello"))` is the very object the literal `"Hello"` refers to, so `canonical(new String("Hello")) == "Hello"` is `true`;
two equal names built at run time come back as the same object;

cases.says: The canonical name has the same text.
canonical(new String("Hello")) is the same object as the literal "Hello".
canonical(null) is null, not a NullPointerException.

concepts: intern() returns the pooled String with the same content, so equal texts become one shared object.
